preview: Sarah: Got it — you knew HD from the Helium project days, liked what they were doing, and now you're testing whether the trust carries over to the mining side.

messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 15 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about a thousand words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, what brought you to HD recently?
I was looking for a solo minor.
Got it — a solo miner. I saw you'd been looking at a few different ones over the past couple months. Let me pull up one of them.
You call it the smoke too hot for smoke out here. Say that again?

Sorry — bit of audio crackle on my end. Let me try again.

You looked at the Bitaxe Gamma a couple times, and also the Lucky Miner LV08 Pro and the Jingle Miner. What was pulling you toward a solo miner in the first place?
One of mine's Bitcoin.
Got it — solo mining for Bitcoin specifically. And why solo versus just pointing at a pool? What's drawing you to the solo route?
The chance of hitting it solo block.

The lottery shot. Makes sense. So when you were comparing the Bitaxe Gamma at $95, the Lucky Miner LV08 Pro at $299, and the Jingle Miner at $319 — what was going through your head? Those are pretty different price points.
Yeah. But they're not too high. Reasonably priced.
Fair — none of them break the bank. But you looked and didn't pull the trigger on any of them. What held you back?
I'm still gonna get it. I'm just doing this survey that y'all asked me to do.
Ah, got it — you're still planning to buy, just haven't yet. That's useful to know. So which one are you leaning toward at this point?
I probably get two or three bit access.
Two or three Bitaxe Gammas — interesting. So stacking the cheaper units instead of going for one of the bigger Lucky Miners or Jingles. Why that direction?
I already have a few bit access at home. But I probably will give it to you. And a couple of ten and six terahash machines.
Oh nice — so you already have a few Bitaxes running at home, plus some 10 and 6 terahash machines. You've got a real little setup going. What are the 10 TH and 6 TH machines — what brands?
ASL. I'm not sure what the other name of the other one is.
Got it. So with that fleet already running, why add more Bitaxes instead of going bigger — like jumping to something with more hashrate per unit?
I have seventeen Casper miners. Twenty terahash, and two forty terahash. Casper miners.

Whoa — okay, so you've got serious firepower already. Seventeen Casper miners, mix of 20 TH and a couple 40 TH. That's a real operation. So where do the little Bitaxes fit into a setup like that? They're like a rounding error on your hashrate.

I'm a use them, and then I buy them, and then I give them away to different people. So that we can scale out Bitcoin and decentralized the network. I'm talking to AI for fifteen minutes, and I'll make seventy five dollars.
Ha — yes, you've got the deal right, $75 code at the end. And honestly what you just said is gold — you're buying Bitaxes to give away, to decentralize the network. That's a really different
That's very nice of them.
It is — and it's a pretty rare reason to buy. Most folks buy for themselves. So who are you giving them to? Friends, family, people online?
This friends family, neighbors, people that I know.
That's awesome. And when you hand one to a friend or a neighbor — what's the conversation? Are they already curious about Bitcoin, or are you basically onboarding them from scratch?
Alright. Some of them know what they are. And a couple of people just brand new. Just getting one. They never ever done anything with mining or anything like that.
So you're literally onboarding people into mining one Bitaxe at a time. That's beautiful. For the brand-new folks — what's the hardest part of getting them set up? Like, where do they get stuck?

Always get stuck when they're trying to configure the machine with their hand on that. The settings, But there was a easier way like an app or something so that or a website. You just go to the website, take their bid ax, or whatever machine it is that they had, and then be able to log straight into a node on the website. Kinda like Casper, the, uh, public network the public node network for that Casper just set up.

Okay, that's really concrete — the wallet config and pool setup is where everyone trips. And you're describing something like a hosted node service — point your Bitaxe at a website, log in, done. Like what Casper just rolled out. Has anyone in the Bitcoin space done that yet, that you've seen?
Not that I know. It'd be nice if Gillian deploy would do that. That would draw more. Attention to your website. And make it easy for people to set up.

That's a really sharp product idea — and I'll make sure it gets to the founders verbatim. "HD-hosted pool / node service so a new buyer just logs in and points their Bitaxe at it." Has anyone you've gifted a Bitaxe to actually given up because the setup was too hard?
I did too, but yes. I've had about three people that have given up. They don't want anything else to do with it.

Three people gave up. That's painful — you bought the hardware, did the gift, and they bounced because of config friction. Do you remember what specifically blocked them? Like was it the wallet address, the pool URL, the wifi setup?
It was the Wi Fi setup. Trying to set up with two point four gigahertz, and a lot of people don't understand that they can split their networks at home.

Yeah — the 2.4 vs 5 GHz thing. Most home routers default to a single SSID and people have no idea their phone is on 5 GHz while the Bitaxe needs 2.4. That's such a specific friction point. Did you end up walking those three through it in person, or was it all remote?
It was all remote.
Remote — so you're basically doing tech support over text or a call. Brutal. Okay, let me switch gears for a sec — have you seen this one — the NerdQaxe Rev 6.1?
No. I have not seen this one.
Okay — it's $249, does 6 TH/s. So roughly 4x the hashrate of a Bitaxe Gamma for about 2.5x the price. Take a sec to look at it — what's your gut reaction?

Well, I think I wanna use my seventy five dollars once I complete this survey, and then I can purchase that one, which that is why I'm doing this survey. So that I can get that. Yes. I have seen that. Before. Sorry about that. My slow phone is dark.

No worries at all — and yes, you'll get the $75 code, you can absolutely put it toward the NerdQaxe. So you have seen it before. What made you not pull the trigger earlier? You were on the site looking at the Bitaxe and the Jingle, but not this one apparently — or was it on your radar?

I think it threw me off when you said you keep saying by text. Is it BitX? I believe it's pronounced that way. You're pronouncing it as By Tax. It's pronounced Bitas, b I t a x e. Two separate words, but they're together. Two syllable words. Then x.

Ha — fair correction. Bit-axe. Got it, thank you. I'll get it right going forward. So — back to the NerdQaxe. You've seen it before. What's pulling you toward it versus just buying more Bit-axes to give away?
Well, my hope is that one day I do hit a big horn block.
The big horn block. Love it. And the NerdQaxe at 6 TH gives you 4x better lottery odds than a single Bitaxe. Have you ever come close — like found a share that was anywhere near difficulty?
Yes. One time, I did.
Wait, really? Tell me about that. How close did you get, and on which machine?
They were a very. Bit ax. I didn't get anything for it. But it was on a Bidax, though. I think it was a Bidax damage.

A Bitaxe Gamma got you close to a block. That's wild — that's the dream right there, and probably exactly why you keep stacking them. Did you tell people about it? Like did that story make it into your gifting pitch when you hand a Bitaxe to a neighbor?
No. I didn't say anything to it. I wanna keep that private.

Fair enough. Okay — last couple things. You mentioned you'd like an HD-hosted node service. Where else do you shop for mining gear besides HD? Like when you were buying the Caspers, or the 10 and 6 TH machines — where'd those come from?
I bought those from I bought a lot of them from Ice River straight from Ice River from their web And then I bought the forty pair of hats from Dickman. And I got that from Terra. Terra hosting.

Ice River direct, and Tera Hosting for the 40 TH units. Got it. And when you compare those experiences — buying from Ice River direct, from Tera Hosting, and from HD — what does HD do better or worse?
I'm not sure yet. I haven't ordered from you guys yet. This should be my first time ordering.
Oh — got it, this would be your first HD order. That's really useful context. So what made you pick HD this time instead of going back to Ice River or trying somewhere else for the smaller miners?
But Ice River doesn't sell any small minors that you guys have.

Ah — Ice River doesn't carry the small stuff. So HD basically owns the small-miner category for you. Has anyone else even shown up on your radar for Bitaxes and NerdQaxes — like Solo Satoshi, AliExpress, anywhere?
No. I did order one, but I from Altair.
Got it — you ordered one from AliExpress. How did that go? Did it show up working, or...?
Nope. It showed about people's burgers. Good order. Everything worked perfectly fine. It's still running out in my house. It works pretty good.
Okay so AliExpress actually delivered for you — unit showed up, still running.
Storm light. I know it's gray. I see. Say that again?

Sorry — I was just saying it's good that the AliExpress one actually worked out. A lot of folks have horror stories with DOA units from there. So if AliExpress worked fine and is cheaper — what's making you choose HD this time instead of just ordering from AliExpress again?

I don't know. I just came across you guys' site. Uh, it looks like it's looks trustworthy and reasonable, and I've heard good things across your So I figured, why not go with you guys and see what happens?
"Trustworthy" — that's a strong word. What did you hear about HD, and where? Like was it Reddit, YouTube, a friend?

No. It's, um, Helium deploy. I used to follow the project, and I want I like I like what the project is doing. And I just wanna get some machines from you guys and try them out, see if you guys live up to you said. That your trustworthiness is. Fast shipments. That's all.
Got it — you knew HD from the Helium project days, liked what they were doing, and now you're testing whether the trust carries over to the mining side.
